source.notes: ICSE Class IX school assessment paper (school not named). Header prints 'Grade- IX', 'Time: 2 Hours', 'ASSESSMENT- I', 'CHEMISTRY', 'M.M. 80'. No year is printed on the paper; examYear 2024 is taken from the file name (icse-class-9-assessment-1-chemistry-230924-2024, i.e. 23-09-2024). The PDF has no text layer (watermark only); text was OCRed with RapidOCR and corrected against the page images. Section A (40 marks, compulsory) prints only group totals for its six groups (I [15], II-VI [5] each), so each group is kept as one entry with that total. Section B (40 marks): the general instructions say 'Attempt any five questions from Section B' but the Section B heading says 'Attempt any four questions from this sections'; six questions (VII-XII) of 10 marks each are printed, and four of them make up the 40 marks. Section B sub-parts carry printed marks and are split. No answer key is printed; no official answers exist.
source.usage: School examination paper published on icseboard.org (originally icseonline.com); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to where it was obtained. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text:
Choose the correct answers from the given options:
1. In the periodic, the elements of a same group have the same:
(a) Mass number (b) Atomic number (c) Number of electrons (d) Number of valence electrons
2. Which of the following is a deliquescent salt?
(a) CuSO₄ (b) FeCl₃ (c) KCl (d) ZnSO₄
3. Thermal decomposition of sodium carbonate will produce
(a) oxygen (b) sodium hydroxide (c) carbon dioxide (d) no other product
4. Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment discovered
(a) proton (b) electron (c) neutron (d) atomic nucleus
5. The most reactive non-metal is :
(a) Iodine b) Oxygen (c) Fluorine (d) Chlorine
6. In the formation of CCl₄ molecule the nearest noble gas configuration attained by carbon and chlorine respectively are :
(a) argon and neon (b) helium and neon (c) neon and argon (d) helium and argon
7. A brown substance A on heating in air turns black forming another substance B. Substances A and B are:
(a) A = Fe and B = FeO (b) A = Zn and B = ZnO (c) A = Cu and B = CuO (d) A = Pb and B = PbO
8. Atoms combine to attain an electronic configuration similar to their nearest :
(a) metal (b) noble gas (c) non-metal (d) semi metal
9. If a salt on heating gives water vapour, then that salt is :
(a) hygroscpic (b) deliquescent (c) hydrated (d) anhydrous
10. Solid solutions are called :
(a) allotropes (b) isotopes (c) alloys (d) isotones
11. With rise in temperature, the solubility of sodium chloride will :
(a) increase rapidly (b) decrease (c) remains same (d) increase slightly
12. Water acts as a universal solvent because :
(a) it is an organic compound (b) it is polar and has a high dielectric constant (c) it is liquid at room temperature (d) it boils at 100°C
13. The salt which is the cause of hardness in water is:
(a) sodium sulphate (b) magnesium bicarbonate (c) sodium chloride (d) calcium nitrate
14. There are 3 electrons in M shell of an atom. Its atomic number is :
(a) 11 (b) 15 (c) 13 (d) 3
15. The number of elements in the largest period of the periodic table is :
(a) 18 (b) 8 (c) 32 (d) 42
